operational-review.name: Operational Review
operational-review.summary: Logical management arc for reviewing how an operation is running: the situation, the complication that threatens it, the resolution, and the roadmap and action plan that deliver it. Built for operations, program and service reviews where the audience needs a decision and a plan, not a story.

beats.name: Headline
beats.description: Open with the operation under review and the one-sentence conclusion of the whole review, so the audience knows where it is going before the detail starts.

beats.name: Situation
beats.description: Describe how the operation runs today with the few metrics that define it: volume, quality, cost, time. Stick to facts the room will agree with.

beats.name: Complication
beats.description: Name what has changed or is at risk: the trend, constraint or failure that makes the current way of running unsustainable. Quantify the cost of doing nothing.

beats.name: Root Causes
beats.description: Explain why the complication is happening. Separate causes the team controls from those it does not, and point to the evidence for each.

beats.name: Resolution
beats.description: Recommend the change that resolves the complication, with the expected effect on the metrics from the situation slide. One recommendation, stated plainly.

beats.name: Roadmap
beats.description: Lay out the phases that deliver the resolution, with what each phase changes and the milestone that marks it done.

beats.name: Action Plan
beats.description: List the immediate actions with an owner and a due date for each, plus the risks to watch. This is the slide people will screenshot.

beats.name: Decision
beats.description: Close with the decision or support you need from this audience today, and what happens next once you have it.

customer.name: Customer
customer.summary: End customers receiving product demos, onboarding presentations, or business reviews.
customer.description: Customers receiving product demos, onboarding, or business reviews. Speak in their language, focus on the value they realize, keep visuals simple, and use strong product screenshots. Keep chart density low; 10-20 slides.

educate.name: Educate
educate.summary: Teach a concept, process, product, or domain so the audience can use it correctly.
educate.description: Use when the primary job is learning. Structure around concepts, examples, practice, and checks for understanding rather than persuasion or reporting.
educate.outcome: The audience understands the material well enough to apply it.

technical.name: Technical
technical.summary: Precise, evidence-led voice for engineering, research, and product-detail audiences.
technical.description: Lead with the question or claim, then walk through the mechanism and the numbers. Use exact terminology; assume the audience can handle and prefers it. Diagrams, tables, and benchmarks are first-class.
voiceCues: State the claim, then the mechanism, then the evidence.
Use exact terminology — don't soften technical terms for general readability.
Quote benchmarks with conditions (cold/warm, p50/p95/p99, dataset, hardware).
Prefer diagrams and tables over prose paragraphs for structural information.
samplePhrases: p95 inference latency is 38ms on a single A100, down from 312ms on the prior runtime.
We replaced the streaming serializer with a batched protobuf path; throughput rose 4.2× under load.
The result holds for context windows up to 32k tokens; beyond that, see appendix B.

bold.name: Bold
bold.description: A vibrant, high-energy theme with bold colors and a dynamic, attention-grabbing style. Great for presentations that need to stand out.

deep-purple.name: Deep Purple
deep-purple.summary: Purple-led palette for innovation and premium positioning.
deep-purple.description: A focused purple palette for decks that need to feel creative, distinctive, and premium.

burnt-orange.name: Burnt Orange
burnt-orange.summary: Warm orange and red accents for energetic commercial decks.
burnt-orange.description: A warm, high-contrast palette built around burnt orange, red, navy, and gold. It feels active without losing structure.

grandview.name: Grandview
grandview.description: Grandview is a sans serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Grandview Display for headings with Grandview for body text.

impact.name: Impact
impact.description: Impact is a sans serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Impact for headings with Grandview for body text.

cover.name: Cover
cover.summary: The opening slide: title, subtitle and an optional picture.
cover.description: Open a presentation with its subject and a short introduction. Add a picture when it helps establish the context.

text.name: Text
text.summary: Prose. Several blocks sit side by side when short and stack when long.
text.description: Explain one idea in continuous prose. Use paragraphs or flowing blocks for detail that needs to be read in sequence.

chart.name: Chart
chart.summary: One to six charts, with an optional note.
chart.description: Give a chart enough space to show its evidence. Use the title to state the conclusion and labels to explain the measures.

list.name: List
list.summary: Bulleted or numbered points; one long list flows into columns.
list.description: Present several related points in a clear sequence. Use bullets for independent points or numbered items for an ordered list.
